title: Charge-transfer gap size and oxygen hole content as two mechanisms controlling $T_c$ in the Emery model
authors: Eleanor M. O'Callaghan, Nicolas Kowalski, A. -M. S. Tremblay, Giovanni Sordi
abstract: Investigating the drivers of superconducting critical temperature trends in cuprates is crucial for uncovering the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity. Here we study this problem in the canonical model of the copper-oxygen plane, the Emery model, with cellular dynamical mean-field theory. Using the Zaanen-Sawatzky-Allen diagram as a guiding framework, we systematically quantify how the maximum superconducting critical temperature $T_c^{\rm max}$ depends on the copper-oxygen energy distance and on the local repulsion on the copper orbital. Unexpectedly, $T_c^{\rm max}$ is optimized not only near the charge-transfer insulator to metal boundary, consistent with previous findings, but also deep in the charge-transfer regime, revealing an unexplored mechanism. Then we link model parameters to physical observables, identifying the charge-transfer gap size and the oxygen hole content as two mechanisms controlling $T_c^{\rm max}$. $T_c^{\rm max}$ increases monotonically as the oxygen hole content increases and the charge gap size decreases. The oxygen hole content is the dominant variable in varying $T_c^{\rm max}$. Our work provides predictions for proposed realizations of the Emery model with ultracold atoms and a theoretical framework for understanding key experimental trends in hole-doped cuprates.
summary: This work analyzes the Emery model for cuprates to understand what drives high-temperature superconductivity. Using advanced quantum many-body theory (CDMFT), the authors find that $T_c$ is primarily controlled by how much charge resides on the oxygen sites (oxygen hole content) and the size of the charge-transfer gap. This provides a crucial theoretical map for understanding cuprate physics.
main_problem: The study investigates the fundamental mechanisms controlling the superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$) trends observed in high-temperature cuprate superconductors.
main_result: The maximum $T_c$ is controlled by two key electronic structure parameters: the charge-transfer gap size ($\Delta_I$) and the oxygen hole content, with the latter being identified as the dominant variable.
method: The research employs cellular dynamical mean-field theory (CDMFT) to solve the model Hamiltonian at finite temperature, guided by the Zaanen-Sawatzky-Allen diagram.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using the Emery model, which describes the copper-oxygen plane in cuprates. This model incorporates onsite repulsion ($U_d$) on Cu and hopping terms between Cu and O orbitals.
key_observables: Superconducting critical temperature ($T_{max}^c$), charge-transfer gap size ($\Delta_I$), and oxygen hole content.
important_parameters: Copper-oxygen energy distance ($\Delta$), onsite repulsion on Cu orbital ($U_d$), and the doping level (related to hole content).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the charge-transfer insulating regime ($U_d > \Delta$) and utilizes CDMFT approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Zaanen-Sawatzky-Allen diagram mapping out constant lines for $\Delta_I$ and oxygen hole content, alongside isotherms used to determine the gap size.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using the Emery model and CDMFT. It then systematically maps the parameter space using the Zaanen-Sawatzky-Allen diagram to quantify how $T_c^{m max}$ depends on $\Delta$ and $U_d$, culminating in identifying the roles of gap size and hole content.
why_interesting: The explicit connection drawn between model parameters (like charge gap) and macroscopic properties ($T_c$) provides a concrete theoretical framework that can be tested against experimental measurements, including those from ultracold atoms simulations.
